content:
As you hopefully know and value, Lean tries its best not to repeat elaboration steps after making changes in the editor (most recently when starting to type the next tactic as well). 4.33.0-rc1 comes with an experimental cmdline feature that allows for such reuse across invocations of lean as well. To directly quote #13965:

This PR adds experimental CLI flags that cache lean's elaboration state used for in-process incrementality across invocations:

  • --incr-save FILE writes a full snapshot including the states after import and after each command at the end of the run
  • --incr-load FILE reuses such a snapshot at startup, up to the first point of syntactic difference just like incrementality in the language server
    • --incr-header-save FILE writes a cheaper and smaller imports-only snapshot

This interface should be considered "plumbing"; it is up to its user to verify that any read snapshots are in fact still valid, i.e. all imported modules are unchanged. The interface is thus not intended for direct use but indirect use by scripts/harnesses.

Together with the follow-up optimizations, we have seen importing Mathlib speed up by >7x, creating a ~300MB header-only snapshot

Unlike previous incrementality work, this feature is a bit hidden and needs to be used manually - there is no automatic use by e.g. Lake (yet). Thus I wanted to both announce it here and fish for potential use cases. Potential further improvements would depend a lot on the specific circumstances, so please let me know about any feedback.

Sebastian Ullrich said:

no automatic use by e.g. Lake (yet)

To expand on this part, one could imagine specific scenarios where such snapshot support might help - for example, if Lake failed to compile a specific file, there is a good chance a similar state of the file will soon be recompiled and thus a snapshot would be helpful. But I felt this was still too speculative to be included in the first version.

I could imagine an enriched version of git worktree that facilitates the branched style of development/exploration that occurs during Mathlib PR writing (working with stacked or broken apart branches), or with agent assisted proof attempts that build on a partially correct intermediate formalization. IIUC these incremental files would help facilitate a shared trunk for the worktrees.

I'm not sure I completely follow you, could you describe a specific scenario where you would like to see elaboration work reuse? For sharing elaboration results of complete modules, i.e. oleans, across checkouts, the Lake artifact cache is the ideal solution.

Lake artifact cache when working on forks of mathlib with slightly divergent git histories is slowed down by attempting to find matching cache at the specific git commit and then works backwards. And it decompresses the entire corpus. And git worktrees, as separate directories, do not share .lake subdirs, so the decompressed cache ends up being duplicated. Those 3 things cumulatively slow down reuse/sharing. Additionally I might have, locally, partially valid Mathlib in which I've modified an early file. To produce a new lake cloud cache artifact, I have to have a PR open, and wait for an entire Mathlib rebuild (cf other thread re trusted forks). I would imagine having a locally invisible minicache that could be shared. Perhaps you mean that lake exe cache put is what is meant to be used.

I think you are talking about the Mathlib cache here, the new Lake cache is separate and not connected to Mathlib's CI (quite) yet. In any case, perhaps we should move this sub-thread to a new topic? The incrementality feature does not eliminate the need to have oleans for imports available in any way.
